mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days because accommodative monetary policy reduces discount rates and increases liquidity, supporting equity valuations without requiring threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the Rank IC over a 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) declines below 95.0 and consumer spending (RSAFS) weakens below 400,000, it indicates dual economic deterioration in manufacturing and consumption that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances where both INDPRO < 95.0 and RSAFS < 400000, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 6.0%) signals central bank policy accommodation to prevent recession, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, S&P 500 produces negative 5-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 6.0%, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days because strong housing activity signals robust consumer confidence and economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings growth without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST exceeds 700,000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO < 95.0, or the Rank IC over a 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline below 700,000 and consumer spending (RSAFS) weakens below 400,000, it indicates broad economic weakness in housing and consumption sectors that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances where both HOUST < 700000 and RSAFS < 400000, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 230.0), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%) reflects aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 230.0, S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or the Rank IC for the regime-specific signal is below 0.03.
